prelude: This course introduces the students to the three meta landscapes of representation, optimization, and objective for the learning tasks on graph data. Graphs are ubiquitous in almost everything today –in social graphs, large-scale biological systems, road networks, polypharmacy, and user-item relations. Graphs, being non-Euclidean, require different machine-learning approaches. This course starts by exploring graph features for traditional machine learning on graphs and discussing a few noteworthy classical graph ML approaches. The second unit focuses on shallow embedding methods for graphs in general, and then the same for knowledge graphs. The third unit focuses on representation learning using graph neural networks and discusses key algorithms along with extensions like temporal graphs and multi-relational graphs. The fourth unit discusses the deep generative models on the graph and model- building techniques using graph neural networks. The theory input concludes with a discussion on the interdisciplinary applications of Graph Neural Networks, interpretability, and meta-learning perspectives of graph AI.

course_title: Embedded system programming with micro python
prelude: This course introduces learners to the world of embedded systems using MicroPython, a lightweight implementation of Python 3 designed to run on microcontrollers. Students will develop a strong foundation in embedded programming principles using accessible and readable Python code. The course guides students from basic setup and scripting to more advanced interfacing with sensors, hardware protocols, and simple Internet of Things (IoT) applications. Through practical labs, real-world examples, and mini-projects, learners will gain hands-on experience in building responsive and connected embedded systems.

prelude: The rise of video as a dominant medium in digital communication and content creation has made the ability to analyze and understand video data a vital skill in the age of AI. This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the theory and application of video processing and video understanding, spanning low-level video enhancement and segmentation techniques to high-level video analytics such as semantic scene understanding, and vision-language integration. Students will explore cutting-edge techniques in action recognition and vision-language models, with applications in video captioning, anomaly detection, and visual question answering, preparing them for real-world challenges in video analytics and artificial intelligence.
objectives: To introduce the foundational concepts and techniques used in digital video processing including representation formats, compression techniques, resolution and frame rate.

To equip students with techniques for video understanding including object recognition, scene parsing, and semantic analysis. To provide exposure to deep learning-based approaches and modern AI and for video analytics, including action recognition, anomaly detection and vision-language models.
